title: Group A streptococcal pharyngitis with rapid antigen test
encounterNote: 23-year-old female presents with two days of sore throat, fever to 38.4 C, and painful swallowing. She denies cough and nasal congestion. Examination: temperature 38.4 C, tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, and no cough. A rapid antigen detection test for group A streptococcus is positive. Assessment: group A streptococcal pharyngitis. She was prescribed a 10-day course of oral penicillin V and advised on supportive care.
